chunks: A man came to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, I saw in my dream as if I was leaving the city of Kufa in a place I recognized, and as if a ghost made of wood, or a man carved from wood, was on a wooden horse waving his sword, and I was watching him, terrified and panicked.' So he (peace be upon him) said to him, 'You are a man who wants to assassinate a man for his livelihood, so fear Allah Who created you, then will cause you to die.'

The man said, 'I testify that you have been given knowledge and extracted it from its mine. I inform you, O son of the Messenger of Allah, about what you have interpreted for me: indeed, a man from my neighbors came to me and offered me his estate, so I intended to acquire it for a small amount because I knew there was no other seeker for it except me.' So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said, 'And your companion has befriended us rather than our enemies?' He said, 'Yes, O son of the Messenger of Allah, a man of good insight, firm in religion, and I am repenting to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to you from what I intended and meant. So inform me, O son of the Messenger of Allah, if he had been a Nasibi (Hostile One), would it have been permissible for me to assassinate him?'
He (peace be upon him) said, 'Fulfill the trust to the one who entrusted you and sought your advice, even if it is to the killer of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.نَاصِب: Nasibi (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on assassinating a rival if they are a Nasibi according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s ability to discern inner intentions through dreams, specifically regarding a neighbor’s potential betrayal. It establishes a crucial Shia legal principle that fidelity and trustworthiness (amanah) are not contingent on the other party’s sectarian alignment, extending even to the 'Nasibi' or archetypal enemy, exemplified by the killer of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him).
